text:
maria: Ran a long-context stress (32k tokens) yesterday and saw steady mem growth on the KV cache that doesn't plateau. Investigating fragmentation vs. slow reclaim. attaching quick profiler dump and pprof top lines.

maria: perf-bot posted a summary too — baseline +18% resident after 2h compared to 8k baseline. :thinking:

perf-bot: baseline-run-2026-03-15: model=redwood-xt-large, ctx=32768, duration=7200s, rss_start=12.2GB, rss_end=14.4GB

aj: thanks. can you paste the pprof snippet? curious about allocator hotspots vs KV GC time.

maria: sure — snippet below (trimmed):

```
(pprof) top10
Rank  Command  Flat %  Flat  Cum %  Cum
1  kv_cache_alloc  36.2%  2.3s  36.2%  2.3s
2  slab_allocator_alloc  18.1%  1.15s  54.3%  3.45s
3  kv_compact_scan  9.4%  0.6s  63.7%  4.05s
4  memcpy  7.0%  0.44s  70.7%  4.49s
```

maria: looks like alloc churn + compact scanning both show up. allocator spends time splitting/zeroing small blocks.

devin: ok that points to many small allocations. do we have distribution of block sizes in the cache? memory histogram?

maria: yep. sketch: 58% of allocations < 256B, 30% 256-2KB, 12% >2KB. median ~180B.

ryan: wow that explains fragmentation. our current slab bucket sizes are powers-of-two starting at 512B. lots of small objects get rounded up -> internal waste.

aj: two levers: 1) change bucket granularity (introduce 128B bucket, or switch to size classes closer to median), 2) aggressive micro-coalescing of free runs during background idle time. both have perf tradeoffs.

sarah: micro-coalesce sounds less invasive. but might add jitter to tail latency if compaction happens on hot threads. proposal: background coalescer thread with fixed budget (cpu ms/s) and backoff on p99 latency regression.

devin: agree. also consider a "compact-on-evict" fast-path: when freeing a sequence of contiguous slots, attempt local merge if run length > threshold. cheap and avoids global scans.

maria: sketch of threshold heuristic: if contiguous_free_bytes >= 4KB then try coalesce; else favor quick free.

ryan: also we should test a "micro-slab" allocation mode tuned for long-context workloads: smaller slab base (128B) + tighter free lists, but disabled by default. enable via runtime flag: kv.slab_mode=micro for canary.

aj: sample config line:
```
kv.slab_config = {
  "base_size": 128,
  "classes": [128, 192, 256, 384, 512, 768, 1024],
  "max_fragmentation_ratio": 0.15
}
```

aj: question — do we measure reuse distance / temporal locality for slots? if small objects are long-lived but reused, fragmentation tolerable; if short-lived, pooling makes sense.

maria: good point. from alloc traces, small objects are often transient between batches but some keys survive across KV cache hits for 50-200 requests. reuse distance peak around 120s.

devin: so mixed. we should do two things in parallel: A) quick experiment changing bucket granularity to add 128B and 192B classes, B) implement a lightweight background micro-coalescer with configurable CPU budget and eviction-triggered local coalesce. run both against 32k load.

ryan: also keep an eye on compaction scanning cost — in the profile kv_compact_scan shows as 9%. if we switch from full-scan compactor to sampling-guided compaction we can reduce CPU while targeting hot fragmentation zones. idea: maintain per-bucket fragmentation score and sample buckets whose score > threshold.

sarah: tests to run:
- canary A: slab granularity change only
- canary B: micro-coalescer only
- canary C: both on
- canary D: sampling compactor + both

maria: planning canary on next cluster slice (nightly window). will attach the exact experiment harness and metrics dashboards.

devin: one more: consider periodic shrink-to-fit of oversized blocks for long-tail contexts: after long request sequences, try to remap block headers and free trailing slack. risky but worth a benchmark.

aj: agreed but mark as experimental. we need p99 latency gating and a fallback that disables shrink when p99 regresses > 5%

maria: I'll draft a small RFC with perf targets, experiment plan, and rollback rules. trying to keep changes incremental.

ryan: thanks. if you want I'll prototype the micro-slab allocator patch — should be a small delta to bucket table and free list.

maria: that'd be great. tagging a few follow-ups: please add benchmark results as comments in this thread when available. :rocket:

sarah: adding a note to the rollout doc: A/B weights, monitoring, and automatic rollback thresholds.

perf-bot: experiment-scheduled: cluster=slice-7, start=1778090000, duration=4h, variants=A,B,C,D

maria: ack. will collect pprof + heap histograms at 15m intervals.

ryan: cool. thanks team.
